To determine the correct antibiotic for selection, we need to identify the antibiotic resistance genes present in the plasmids used in the Golden Gate cloning reaction. Golden Gate assembly relies on Type IIS restriction enzymes (like Esp3I) that cut outside their recognition site, allowing for the seamless assembly of DNA fragments. The resulting construct will contain the combined sequences of the input plasmids. Therefore, the transformants will be resistant to any antibiotic for which a resistance gene is present in the final assembled plasmid.
